previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with cough, shortness of breath, and fatigue in the setting of relapsed multiple myeloma and recent cytopenias. He had been receiving outpatient radiation for a perivesicular plasmacytoma, which had resolved his prior pain. Imaging showed mild bronchial wall thickening consistent with viral bronchitis, with no pneumonia. He was treated with intravenous and then oral levofloxacin, albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers, and supportive care. His respiratory symptoms improved, white blood cell count recovered, and he completed his prescribed radiation. He was discharged home with a two-week supply of nebulizers, a five-day course of oral antibiotics, and instructions to follow up with his oncology and primary care teams.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with hx of myeloma, prior hx of diverticulitis as
well as paravesicular mass s/p XRT.  Presents today with weakness, profound
anemia, frequent stool and left lower abdominal pain and urinary frequency.

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 4.6 s, 50.4 cm; CTDIvol = 17.0 mGy (Body) DLP = 854.4
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 854 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis ___

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST:  Bibasilar atelectasis.  Otherwise, visualized lung fields are
within normal limits. There is no evidence of pleural or pericardial effusion.
Hyperdensity of interventricular septum is compatible with known anemia.

ABDOMEN:

Lack of IV contrast limits evaluation.

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic
or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is within normal limits.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is an unchanged 0.4 cm nonobstructing nephrolith in the lower pole of
the right kidney (___).  There is no evidence of hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  There is
diverticulosis.  The colon and rectum are otherwise within normal limits.  The
appendix is normal.

PELVIS: The distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is thickening of the
bladder wall, unchanged compared ___, which may in part be
secondary to underdistension.  There is an essentially unchanged paravesicular
mass measuring 5.8 x 3.0 cm (___), previously 5.9 x 3.9 cm.  There is no free
fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The patient is status post prostatectomy.  The visualized
reproductive organs are otherwise unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture. 
Again seen are multiple chronic rib fractures (for example, ___ and an
unchanged compression fracture through the superior endplate of T12. 
Unchanged irregularity of the bilateral inferior pubic rami, dating back to
earliest available study ___.

SOFT TISSUES: There is an unchanged small fat containing right inguinal
hernia.  The patient is status post left inguinal hernia repair.  The
abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION: 

Lack of IV contrast limits evaluation.

1. No evidence of diverticulitis.
2. Compared to ___, no significant change in a paravesicular mass
adjacent to the left wall of the bladder.  This mass was previously biopsied
and shown to represent plasma cell dyscrasia.
3. Unchanged 0.4 cm nonobstructing nephrolith in the lower pole of the right
kidney.
